interest: Shows State and Treasury tracking Japanese financial assets in the U.S. after the December 1937 Panay Incident, including gold shipments.
overview: December 17, 1937 memo for Maxwell Hamilton surveys Japanese liquid resources in the U.S.: $45.2 million in New York bank balances, $233 million in gold shipped since March to build dollar reserves, and about $100 million total in liquid dollar availabilities.

people.name: Maxwell M. Hamilton
people.role: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE), Department of State

people.name: Herbert Feis

subfiles.about: Memorandum detailing Japanese liquid assets, gold shipments, bank balances, and security holdings in the United States as of December 1937.
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs (initials H.S.P.)
subfiles.summary: Memo for Maxwell Hamilton finds Japanese bank balances in New York at $45.2 million by December 8, 1937 (mostly Yokohama Specie Bank), $233 million in gold shipped since March used to build dollar reserves rather than cover trade, and total Japanese liquid dollar availabilities in the U.S. near $100 million.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs to Maxwell M. Hamilton on Japanese Liquid Resources in the United States
subfiles.to: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Chief of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE)
